blog_post.body:
## What does instant coffee label mean for an Indian kitchen?

When you pick up a jar at the grocery store, the small print on the back tells the real story of what is sitting in your pantry. Many commercial brands mix in chicory root to stretch the yield, which is why Ultra Blend contains 70% coffee and 30% chicory for a milder, budget-friendly cup. But if you prefer pure coffee with zero fillers, options like Bold offer an honest kick at ₹369 for 100g, while freeze-dried choices like Purica bring pure Arabica straight to your mug. Reading the fine print helps you understand exactly what you are brewing every morning. A clear ingredient list means no surprises, letting you choose between a smooth everyday blend or pure coffee without wondering what else made it into the jar. At Purity Beans, transparency is simple: every label clearly states what is inside so you always know what you are pouring into your morning cup.

### A plain definition

Whatever brought you here, the label settles it. The other single jars on this page are 0% chicory.

## How do you read the chicory line on the jar?

When you pick up a jar of instant coffee, the most important place to look isn’t the flashy branding on the front—it’s the ingredient list tucked away on the back. Many commercial brands mix in chicory root, a woody root substitute, to bulk up the volume and cut down on production costs.
